speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand what is happening during these episodes, can you describe exactly what happens right before you become unresponsive? Also, does anyone notice rhythmic jerking movements or eye deviation during these spells?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does he have any history of head trauma, fever, or seizures in the family? Do these episodes occur more frequently during sleep or while he is awake?

speaker: Patient
text: c and confused afterwards. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That assessment is highly unlikely given the semiology of a focal aware seizure with an oral aura and post-ictal confusion. REQUEST TEST: EEG with sleep deprivation.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The EEG findings confirm a diagnosis of right temporal lobe epilepsy, which aligns perfectly with the oral aura, automatisms, and post-ictal confusion. DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Temporal Lobe Epilepsy
